claims.statement: In Belarusian mythology Vyal is one of the tsmoki (dragons); his legend was recorded by Iryna Dubianetskaya in the village of Valeikishki (Astravets district).
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Belarus, Vyal adalah salah satu cmok (naga); legendanya dicatat oleh Iryna Dubianetskaya di desa Valeikishki (distrik Astravets).
claims.quote: Вяль — у беларускай міфалогіі адзін з цмокаў. Паданне аб ім запісана Ірынай Дубянецкай у в. Валэйкішкі (Астравецкі раён).

claims.statement: Vyal lived by a boulder near the village of Valeikishki, played with it, tossed it about, kept people from passing and stole their cattle.
claims.statement_id: Vyal tinggal di dekat sebuah batu besar dekat desa Valeikishki, bermain-main dengan batu itu, melemparkannya, menghalangi orang lewat, dan mencuri ternak mereka.
claims.quote: Вяль жыў каля валуна бліз вёскі Валэйкішкі, бавіўся з ім, перакідваў і не даваў людзям прайсці, а таксама краў у іх скаціну.

claims.statement: One day a clever villager slaughtered a ram, skinned it, filled the skin with "tar and sulphur" and set it by the stone; the tsmok saw the "ram" and ate it at once.
claims.statement_id: Suatu hari seorang penduduk desa yang cerdik menyembelih seekor domba jantan, menguliti dan mengisi kulitnya dengan "ter dan belerang", lalu menaruhnya di dekat batu; sang cmok melihat "domba" itu dan langsung memakannya.
claims.quote: Аднойчы разумны вясковец закалоў барана, злупіў з яго скуру, заліў у яе «смалу і серку» і паставіў каля камня. Цмок убачыў «барана» і адразу з’еў.

claims.statement: Hot tar filled his throat and he died at once; before dying Vyal roared so loudly that the tsmok Krok, who lived near Kraków, heard him and himself died of fright.
claims.statement_id: Ter panas memenuhi tenggorokannya dan ia langsung mati; sebelum mati Vyal meraung begitu keras sehingga terdengar oleh cmok Krok yang tinggal dekat Kraków, yang ikut mati ketakutan.
claims.quote: Гарачая смала заліла яму глотку, і ён адразу памёр. Перад смерцю Вяль зароў так громка, што яго пачуў цмок Крок, што жыў пад Кракавам, і сам адразу памёр са страху.

claims.statement: The name Vyal points to the names of Baltic gods who guard the dead and the underworld: Vels among the Latvians, Velinas among the Lithuanians, and also Veles, whose name is genetically related.
claims.statement_id: Nama Vyal merujuk pada nama dewa-dewa Balt pelindung orang mati dan dunia bawah: Vels pada orang Latvia, Velinas pada orang Lituania, serta Veles yang namanya berasal-usul sama.
claims.quote: Імя Вяль адсылае да імёнаў балцкіх багоў-апекуноў памерлых і падзем’я: Vels у латышоў, Velinas у літоўцаў, а таксама Вялеса, імя якога генетычна да іх узыходзіць.

claims.statement: In Poland there is a legend of the Wawel Dragon, who lived in a hill near Kraków and was destroyed in the same way as Vyal.
claims.statement_id: Di Polandia ada legenda tentang Naga Wawel yang tinggal di bukit dekat Kraków dan dibinasakan dengan cara yang sama seperti Vyal.
claims.quote: У Польшчы захавалася легенда пра Вавельскага цмока, які жыў у прыгорку пад Кракавам і быў знішчаны гэтакім жа чынам, як і Вяль

claims.statement: In Iryna Dubianetskaya's telling, the dragon lived near a locality, played with a big stone and kept people from passing; that was the only bad thing it did in this story.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penuturan Iryna Dubianetskaya, naga itu tinggal dekat sebuah tempat, bermain dengan batu besar dan menghalangi orang lewat; hanya itu perbuatan buruknya dalam kisah ini.
claims.quote: Каля нейкай беларускай мясцовасці жыў цмок, што бавіўся з вялікім каменем і не даваў людзям прайсці. Гэта адзінае, што ён рабіў кепскага ў гэтай гісторыі.

claims.statement: Dubianetskaya recorded this legend of the dragon named Vyal (Вяль) in the village of Valeikishki (Валэйкішкі) in the Astravets area; local people link the village's name to the dragon's name.
claims.statement_id: Dubianetskaya mencatat legenda tentang naga bernama Vyal (Вяль) ini di desa Valeikishki (Валэйкішкі) di wilayah Astravets; penduduk setempat mengaitkan nama desa itu dengan nama naga tersebut.
claims.quote: А цмока звалі Вяль. Гэтую легенду я запісала ў вёсцы Валэйкішкі на Астравеччыне. Мясцовыя жыхары звязваюць назву вёскі менавіта з імем цмока.

claims.statement: According to Dubianetskaya, similar legends are fairly widespread in Belarus (Беларусі).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Dubianetskaya, legenda serupa cukup tersebar di Belarus (Беларусі).
claims.quote: І таксама здох са страху”. Аналагічныя легенды досыць пашыраныя ў Беларусі.

claims.statement: Wars and Sawa are legendary characters of the origin myth of the founding and name of Warsaw, capital of Poland; there are several versions of the legend.
claims.statement_id: Wars dan Sawa adalah tokoh legenda dalam mitos asal-usul pendirian dan nama kota Warsawa, ibu kota Polandia; legenda kemunculan mereka punya beberapa versi.
claims.quote: are legendary characters from the origin myth of the founding and etymology of the city of Warsaw, capital of Poland. There are several versions of the legend with their appearance.

claims.statement: In one version a duke or king named Kazimierz (Casimir), sometimes identified as Duke Siemowit I of Masovia, got lost while hunting in the forest where Warsaw Old Town now stands.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu versi, seorang adipati atau raja bernama Kazimierz (Casimir), kadang disamakan dengan Adipati Siemowit I dari Masovia, tersesat saat berburu di hutan tempat Kota Tua Warsawa kini berada.
claims.quote: According to one version of the legend, the duke or king called Kazimierz (Casimir), sometimes also identified as duke Siemowit I of Masovia, got lost in the forest, where Warsaw Old Town is currently located, while hunting.

claims.statement: He came upon a small adobe hut where a woman had just given birth to twins; she hosted him generously, and he named the children Wars and Sawa and gave her money to build a bigger house.
claims.statement_id: Ia menemukan pondok bata lumpur kecil yang dihuni seorang perempuan yang baru melahirkan bayi kembar; perempuan itu menjamunya dengan murah hati, lalu ia menamai kedua anak itu Wars dan Sawa dan memberi uang untuk membangun rumah yang lebih besar.
claims.quote: He came across a small adobe hut, inhabited by a woman who had recently given birth to twins. The woman hosted him very generously. He named her two children Wars and Sawa and gave the woman money to build a bigger house.

claims.statement: Later others settled near the house, forming a settlement named after the twins, Warsawa, which became Warszawa, the Polish name of Warsaw.
claims.statement_id: Kemudian orang lain pindah ke dekat rumah itu dan membentuk permukiman bernama Warsawa menurut nama si kembar, yang kemudian berubah menjadi Warszawa, nama kota Warsawa dalam bahasa Polandia.
claims.quote: Later, other people moved near the house, forming a settlement, which was named after the twins, Warsawa, which later evolved to Warszawa, the name of the city of Warsaw in the Polish language.

claims.statement: In a different version Wars and Sawa were a married couple living in that house who hosted the duke.
claims.statement_id: Menurut versi lain, Wars dan Sawa adalah pasangan suami istri yang tinggal di rumah itu dan menjamu sang adipati.
claims.quote: According to a different version of the legend, Wars and Sawa were a married couple who lived in that house, and who hosted the duke.

claims.statement: In another version Sawa was a mermaid living in the Vistula river with whom a fisherman named Wars fell in love.
claims.statement_id: Menurut versi lain lagi, Sawa adalah putri duyung yang tinggal di Sungai Vistula dan dicintai seorang nelayan bernama Wars.
claims.quote: According to another version of the legend, Sawa was a mermaid living in the Vistula river with whom a fisherman named Wars fell in love.

claims.statement: In yet another version Wars and Sawa were brothers, fishermen living near today's Warsaw Old Town.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi lainnya, Wars dan Sawa adalah dua bersaudara nelayan yang tinggal di dekat Kota Tua Warsawa sekarang.
claims.quote: In yet another version of the legend, Wars and Sawa were brothers, who were fishermen living near modern Warsaw Old Town.

claims.statement: There is a statue of Wars and Sawa in Warsaw Old Town (Brzozowa Street).
claims.statement_id: Di Kota Tua Warsawa (Jalan Brzozowa) terdapat patung Wars dan Sawa.
claims.quote: Statue of Wars and Sawa in the Warsaw Old Town (Brzozowa Street).

claims.statement: According to another version, Warsz and Sawa were brothers, fishermen living on the Vistula (Wisła) at the foot of the New Town (Nowe Miasto).
claims.statement_id: Menurut versi lain, Warsz dan Sawa adalah dua bersaudara nelayan yang tinggal di tepi Sungai Vistula (Wisła), di kaki Kota Baru (Nowe Miasto).
claims.quote: Według innej wersji Warsz i Sawa byli braćmi, rybakami mieszkającymi nad Wisłą, u podnóża Nowego Miasta

claims.statement: In this version, by the riverbank behind the reeds the duke saw a water maiden (panna wodna) holding a yew bow.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi ini, di tepi sungai di balik alang-alang sang adipati melihat seorang putri air (panna wodna) yang memegang busur dari kayu yew.
claims.quote: Przy brzegu, za trzcinami, ujrzał pannę wodną. W rękach miała cisowy łuk.

claims.statement: The mermaid (Syrena) drew her bowstring and loosed a golden arrow, and the duke followed its track.
claims.statement_id: Sang putri duyung (Syrena) menarik tali busurnya dan melepaskan anak panah emas, lalu sang adipati mengikuti arahnya.
claims.quote: Syrena napięła cięciwę łuku, a wypuszczona złota strzała poszybowała przed siebie. Jej tropem podążył książę.

claims.statement: Moved by the poor couple's hospitality, Siemowit decided to become godfather to their children and named them Warsz and Sawa.
claims.statement_id: Tersentuh oleh keramahan pasangan miskin itu, Siemowit memutuskan menjadi ayah baptis anak-anak mereka dan menamai mereka Warsz dan Sawa.
claims.quote: Siemowit wzruszony gościnnością ubogiej pary postanowił zostać ojcem chrzestnym ich dzieci. Nadał im imiona Warsz i Sawa

claims.statement: Only the Syrena, patroness of the future city, knew that the duke's promises would come true.
claims.statement_id: Hanya Syrena, pelindung kota yang akan datang, yang tahu bahwa janji sang adipati akan terwujud.
claims.quote: I tylko Syrena, uśmiechająca się do niej patronka przyszłego miasta, wiedziała, że tak się stanie.

claims.statement: This retelling is based on Ewa Szelburg-Zarembina's legend "Wróżba panny wodnej".
claims.statement_id: Penceritaan ulang ini disusun berdasarkan legenda karya Ewa Szelburg-Zarembina, "Wróżba panny wodnej".
claims.quote: Tekst powstał na podstawie legendy Ewy Szelburg-Zarembiny „Wróżba panny wodnej”

claims.statement: The kasny are evil spirits that act in groups.
claims.statement_id: Kasny adalah roh jahat yang bertindak berkelompok.
claims.quote: Кáсны — ліхія духі, якія дзейнічаюць гуртам.

claims.statement: The name kasny may be related to the Belarusian dialect word kasny "shameful, bad, thin" and the Russian dialect kastnyi, kastnoi "vile, disgusting, ugly, unclean".
claims.statement_id: Nama kasny mungkin berkaitan dengan kata dialek Belarus "kasny" (memalukan, buruk, kurus) dan kata dialek Rusia "kastnyi, kastnoi" (keji, menjijikkan, jelek, najis).
claims.quote: Назва касны магчыма звязана з беларускім дыялектным касны «сараматны, дрэнны, худы», рускім дыялектным кáстный, кастнóй «паскудны, гідкі, брыдкі, нячысты»

claims.statement: Having attacked a victim, they suck onto it like leeches until it dies; the more the victim resists, the harder they cling, as if seized by malice.
claims.statement_id: Setelah menyerang korban, mereka menempel dan mengisapnya seperti lintah sampai korban mati; makin korban melawan, makin kuat mereka melekat, seolah dikuasai amarah.
claims.quote: Напаўшы на ахвяру, прысмоктваюцца да яе, нібы п’яўкі, пакуль тая не памрэ. Чым больш ахвяра супраціўляецца, тым з большай сілаю яны прыстаюць да яе, нібы ахопленыя злобай.

claims.statement: If only one kasny clings there is nothing to fear; but if two or three attack, while one stays by the victim the others can summon more.
claims.statement_id: Jika hanya satu kasny yang menempel, tidak ada yang perlu ditakuti; tetapi jika dua atau tiga menyerang, selagi satu di dekat korban, yang lain bisa memanggil kawan-kawannya.
claims.quote: Калі прыстае адзін з каснаў, то баяцца няма чаго. Калі ж напад зроблены двума-трыма каснамі, то пакуль адзін ля ахвяры, астатнія могуць склікаць іншых.

claims.statement: A victim can hear their squeaking only when carrying the amulet called "Thursday salt", salt blessed in church on Maundy Thursday.
claims.statement_id: Korban hanya bisa mendengar cicitan mereka bila membawa jimat "garam Kamis", yaitu garam yang diberkati di gereja pada Kamis Putih.
claims.quote: Іх піск ахвяра можа пачуць толькі маючы пры сабе такі абярэг як «чацвярговая соль» — гэта значыць соль, асвечаная ў храме на Чысты чацвер.

claims.statement: These unclean beings share traits with other bloodsuckers such as the vupyr and eretnik.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk najis ini punya ciri yang sama dengan pengisap darah lain seperti vupyr dan eretnik.
claims.quote: Гэтыя нячысцікі маюць агульныя рысы з іншымі крывасмокамі: вупырамі, ератнікамі.

claims.statement: According to Nikiforovsky, in outward appearance the kasny (касны) seem smaller than the sheshki (шешекъ), but are far cleverer, more persistent and always act in a pack.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Nikiforovsky, dari rupa luarnya kasny (касны) tampak lebih kecil daripada šeški (шешекъ), tetapi jauh lebih cerdik, lebih gigih, dan selalu bertindak berkawanan.
claims.quote: По внЪшнему облику касны какъ будто меньше шешекъ, но гораздо толковће ихъ, болфе настойчивы и дйствують непре- мЪнно скопомъ

claims.statement: Rage intoxicates the kasny so that they no longer even feel the people's means of rescue, that is, being struck with consecrated objects.
claims.statement_id: Amarah memabukkan kasny sehingga mereka bahkan tidak lagi merasakan sarana penyelamat manusia, yaitu pukulan dengan benda-benda yang diberkati.
claims.quote: Злоба опьяняетъ касновъ: они даже перестають чув- ствовать воздЪйстве спасательныхъ людскихъ средствъ— поражеше освященными предметами.

claims.statement: As a result some kasny perish or are maimed while attacking, or perish together with the victim, not letting go even after stronger unclean spirits have long withdrawn; together with their weak fertility, this leads to their gradual decline.
claims.statement_id: Akibatnya sebagian kasny binasa atau cedera saat menyerang, atau binasa bersama korbannya karena tidak mau melepaskannya bahkan setelah roh-roh jahat yang lebih kuat sudah pergi; ditambah kesuburan mereka yang rendah, hal ini membuat jumlah mereka berangsur berkurang.
claims.quote: Сл$дстыемъ сего бываеть, что отдфль- ные касны гибнуть, или увфчатся еще во время приставаній, гибнуть и вмЪст съ жертвою, оть которой иные не отстаютъ тогда, когда довершивиие гибель ея боле сильные нечистики давно отступили прочь. А это, въ соединеній со слабою плодо- витостью касновъ, ведеть къ постепенному уменьшению ихъ.

claims.statement: The hartsuki are characters proposed by P. Shpilevsky: black spirits subject to Perun; their name comes from the word "hartsavats" (to frolic, to race).
claims.statement_id: Hartsuki adalah tokoh yang diajukan oleh P. Shpilevsky: roh-roh hitam yang tunduk kepada Perun; namanya berasal dari kata "hartsavats" (bermain, berlari berlomba).
claims.quote: Гарцукі — прапанаваныя П. Шпілеўскім персанажы, чорныя духі, падначаленыя Перуну. Іх імя паходзіць ад слова «гарцаваць» — гуляць, бегаць навыперадкі.

claims.statement: In this description they live in great mountains and play like children at sunrise and sunset; at noon they dash on horseback across fields and forests, and at night, on Perun's orders, fly through the air in the form of various birds of prey.
claims.statement_id: Menurut gambaran itu, mereka tinggal di gunung-gunung besar dan bermain seperti anak-anak saat matahari terbit dan terbenam; siang hari mereka melesat berkuda melintasi ladang dan hutan, dan malam hari atas perintah Perun terbang di udara dalam wujud berbagai burung pemangsa.
claims.quote: Жывуць яны ў вялікіх гарах, дзе падчас усходу і заходу сонца гуляюць, нібы дзеці. Апоўдні стралою носяцца на конях па палях і лясах, а ўначы па даручэнні Перуна лятаюць у паветры, набываючы аблічча розных драпежных птушак.

claims.statement: The hartsuki haul the thunder millstone across the sky, on which Perun rides with a fiery bow; they raise winds, storms, whirlwinds and other natural phenomena.
claims.statement_id: Hartsuki menarik batu gilingan guntur melintasi langit, yang ditunggangi Perun dengan busur berapi; mereka menimbulkan angin, badai, pusaran angin, dan gejala alam lainnya.
claims.quote: Гарцукі возяць па небе грамавы жоран, на якім раз’язджае Пярун з вогненным лукам; яны ўтвараюць вятры, буру і віхры і іншыя стыхійныя прыродныя з’явы.

claims.statement: These characters are mentioned only in the texts of the ethnographer Pavel Shpilevsky; later researchers noted that Belarusian peasants had heard nothing of them and that Shpilevsky may simply have invented them.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh-tokoh ini hanya disebut dalam teks etnograf Pavel Shpilevsky; peneliti kemudian mencatat bahwa petani Belarus tidak pernah mendengar tentang mereka dan bahwa Shpilevsky mungkin hanya mengarangnya.
claims.quote: Персанажы згаданы толькі ў тэктах этнографа Паўла Шпілеўскага. Пазнейшыя даследчыкі заўважалі, што беларускія сяляне нічога не чулі пра гэтых персанажаў і што Шпілеўскі, магчыма, проста іх выдумаў.

claims.statement: Pavel Shpilevsky is known for numerous falsifications of myths and folklore.
claims.statement_id: Pavel Shpilevsky dikenal karena banyak memalsukan mitos dan cerita rakyat.
claims.quote: Павел Шпілеўскі вядомы шматлікімі фальсіфікацыямі міфаў і фальклора.

claims.statement: The interviewee explains that according to the author the hartsuki (гарцукоў) are helpers of Perun (Перуна), spirits flying in the sky and carrying out his errands; yet in 200 years of Belarusian ethnography nobody recorded even similar characters, so the writer most likely invented them.
claims.statement_id: Narasumber wawancara menjelaskan bahwa menurut sang pengarang, hartsuki (гарцукоў) adalah pembantu Perun (Перуна), roh yang terbang di langit dan menjalankan perintahnya; namun selama 200 tahun etnografi Belarus tidak ada yang mencatat tokoh serupa, sehingga kemungkinan besar sang penulis mengarangnya.
claims.quote: — Вазьміце гарцукоў: паводле аўтара, гэта памочнікі Перуна, духі, якія лётаюць па небе і выконваюць яго даручэнні. Аднак за 200 гадоў беларускай этнаграфіі больш ніхто нідзе не фіксаваў хаця б падобных персанажаў, інфармацыі пра іх — нуль. Адкуль пісьменнік іх узяў? Хутчэй за ўсё проста прыдумаў.

claims.statement: This is why the hartsuki (гарцукоў) and other characters that never existed in native folklore reappear on book pages.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu hartsuki (гарцукоў) dan tokoh lain yang tidak pernah ada dalam folklor Belarus muncul lagi di halaman-halaman buku.
claims.quote: Таму на старонках ізноў бачым гарцукоў і іншых персанажаў, якія ніколі не існавалі ў айчынным фальклоры.

claims.statement: The Rain Bull (bg: Dazhdoven bivol) is an episodic character in some San (Bushman) myths; his main duty is to bring rain to the earth, which he does with pleasure and joy.
claims.statement_id: Banteng Hujan (bg: Dazhdoven bivol) adalah tokoh sampingan dalam beberapa mitos orang San (Bushmen); tugas utamanya membawa hujan ke bumi, dan ia melakukannya dengan senang hati.
claims.quote: Дъждовен бивол е епизодичен персонаж в някои бушменски митове. Основното му задължение е да носи дъжд на земята. Изпълнява тази задача с удоволствие и радост.

claims.statement: He lives in the sky but sometimes comes down among people; he usually dwells in lakes, and wherever he heads, rain falls there.
claims.statement_id: Ia tinggal di langit tetapi kadang turun ke tengah manusia; biasanya ia tinggal di danau, dan ke mana pun ia pergi, di sana turun hujan.
claims.quote: Той живее на небето, но понякога слиза и при хората. Обикновено живее в езерата, а когато се запъти нанякъде, там, накъдето се е отправил, завалява дъжд.

claims.statement: If they see him, the San follow him with all their belongings to find land rich in sweet roots and game.
claims.statement_id: Jika melihatnya, orang San mengikutinya dengan seluruh barang bawaan untuk menemukan tanah yang kaya akar manis dan hewan buruan.
claims.quote: Ако го видят, бушмените го следват с целия си багаж за да намерят земя, богата на сладки корени и дивеч.

claims.statement: In the myth of Kua and the Rain Bull, the rain once came down to earth in the form of the Rain Bull.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos Kua dan Banteng Hujan, suatu kali hujan turun ke bumi dalam wujud Banteng Hujan.
claims.quote: Веднъж дъждът слязъл на земята приемайки формата на Дъждовния бик.

claims.statement: He found Kua, a young woman lying gravely ill, while her sister tried to help her.
claims.statement_id: Ia menemukan Kua, perempuan muda yang terbaring sakit parah, sementara saudarinya berusaha menolongnya.
claims.quote: Това била Куа, която лежала тежко болна, а край нея се въртяла сестра ѝ и се опитвала да ѝ помогне.

claims.statement: The sister rubbed leaves of the herb buchu (Agathosma betulina) and scattered them around Kua's body to heal her.
claims.statement_id: Saudarinya menggosok daun herba buchu (Agathosma betulina) dan menaburkannya di sekitar tubuh Kua untuk menyembuhkannya.
claims.quote: Сестрата разтривала листа от билката бучу (Agathosma betulina) и ги разпръсквала около тялото на Куа, опитвайки се да я излекува.

claims.statement: The sight of the suffering young woman filled the Rain Bull's heart with pity, and he quietly began to sing one of his magic healing songs.
claims.statement_id: Melihat perempuan muda yang menderita itu, hati Banteng Hujan dipenuhi iba, dan ia mulai menyanyikan pelan salah satu lagu penyembuh ajaibnya.
claims.quote: Гледката на младата страдаща жена изпълнило сърцето на Дъждовния бик със съчувствие и болка. Той тихичко започнал да пее една от вълшебните си целебни песни.

claims.statement: Gradually the illness left her; she rose, took her child from her sister's arms and rocked it.
claims.statement_id: Perlahan penyakitnya hilang; Kua bangkit, mengambil bayinya dari tangan saudarinya, dan menimangnya.
claims.quote: Постепенно болестта започнала да я напуска, тя се изправила, взела детето от ръцете на сестра си и го залюляла.

claims.statement: Finally, at a clear spring, he realised he had found his home, from which to send life-giving rain over all the earth for every living creature.
claims.statement_id: Akhirnya di sebuah mata air jernih ia sadar telah menemukan rumahnya, tempat ia mengirim hujan pemberi hidup ke seluruh bumi bagi semua makhluk.
claims.quote: Разбрал, че е намерил своя дом, откъдето да изпраща животворен дъжд по цялата земя за всички живи създания.

claims.statement: Kua climbed onto his back and scattered some of the herbs on his head; he felt happy and elated and trotted off with Kua on his back.
claims.statement_id: Kua naik ke punggungnya dan menaburkan sebagian herba ke kepalanya; sang banteng merasa bahagia dan bersemangat, lalu berlari kecil membawa Kua di punggungnya.
claims.quote: Качила се на гърба му и разпръснала част от билките върху главата му. От всичко това той се почувствал щастлив и въодушевен, обърнал се и потеглил в тръс с Куа на гърба си.

claims.statement: In the tale recorded by Bleek and Lloyd, a young woman was in her hut because she was still ill; the Rain scented her and went forth on account of it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat Bleek dan Lloyd, seorang perempuan muda berada di pondoknya karena masih sakit; Hujan (the Rain) mencium baunya lalu keluar karenanya.
claims.quote: while the young woman was in (her) hut, because she felt that she was still ill. The Rain scented her, and the Rain went forth, on account of it;

claims.statement: According to a footnote to the tale, the Rain resembled a bull.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan kaki kisah itu, Hujan menyerupai seekor banteng (bull).
claims.quote: He resembled a bull, while he felt that (he) was the Rain's

claims.statement: The young woman took up buchu and threw it upon his forehead.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan muda itu mengambil buchu dan melemparkannya ke dahi Banteng Hujan.
claims.quote: The young woman took up buchu in her hand, the young woman threw buchu upon his forehead.

claims.statement: She mounted the Rain, and the Rain took her away.
claims.statement_id: Ia menaiki Hujan, dan Hujan membawanya pergi.
claims.quote: She mounted the Rain; and the Eain took her away.

claims.statement: She laid her child down because she thought she would die and go to become a frog.
claims.statement_id: Ia meletakkan anaknya karena mengira dirinya akan mati dan berubah menjadi katak (frog).
claims.quote: She laid it down, while she thought that she should die, (and) go to become a frog.

claims.statement: According to the people quoted, when the Rain's Bull goes out of his pit, the water pit dries up.
claims.statement_id: Menurut orang San yang dikutip, ketika Banteng Hujan (the Rain's Bull) keluar dari lubang airnya, lubang itu menjadi kering.
claims.quote: the pit becomes dry, while it feels that the Rain has gone out, the Rain's Bull. Therefore, the pit dries up on account of it.

claims.statement: The kenchrines is a mythical monster inhabiting the Thracian islands of the Aegean Sea, mentioned by Nicander.
claims.statement_id: Kenchrines adalah monster mitos yang menghuni pulau-pulau Thrakia di Laut Aegea, disebut oleh Nikandros (Nicander).
claims.quote: Кенхринес (kenchrines) – митично чудовище, обитаващо тракийските острови в Егейско море, споменато от Никандър.

claims.statement: Also called the "spotted lion" (or "lion speckled with scales"), it is a huge snake, probably with a lion's head.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga disebut "singa belang" (atau "singa bertotol sisik") dan berupa ular raksasa, kemungkinan berkepala singa.
claims.quote: Наричано още „шарен лъв“ (или „пропъстрен с люспи лъв“), то представлява огромна змия, вероятно с лъвска глава.

claims.statement: The kenchrines kills with a strong venom that rots the skin, eats away the joints and causes severe stomach pain, or by coiling round and strangling its victim and sucking its blood.
claims.statement_id: Kenchrines membunuh dengan racun kuat yang membusukkan kulit, menggerogoti sendi, dan menimbulkan sakit perut hebat, atau dengan melilit dan mencekik korbannya lalu mengisap darahnya.
claims.quote: Кенхринес убива със силна отрова, причиняваща загнивания на кожата, разяждане на ставите и силни стомашни болки или обвивайки и задушавайки жертвата си и изсмуква кръвта ѝ.

claims.statement: It attacks at noon, its victims usually being sheep resting at midday unattended by their shepherds, but it is deadly to humans as well.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyerang pada tengah hari, biasanya memangsa domba yang beristirahat siang tanpa diawasi penggembala, tetapi juga mematikan bagi manusia.
claims.quote: Напада по пладне, като жертвите му обикновено са пладнуващи овце, оставени без надзор от пастирите си, но е смъртно опасно и за човека.

claims.statement: Nicander calls the kenchrines (κεγχρίνεω) a long monster (δολιχὸν τέρας), named the "spotted lion" (λέοντα αἰόλον) and dotted all over with scales (περίστικτον φολίδεσσι).
claims.statement_id: Nikandros menyebut kenchrines (κεγχρίνεω) sebagai makhluk ajaib yang panjang (δολιχὸν τέρας), yang dinamai "singa berbintik" (λέοντα αἰόλον) dan berbintik-bintik sisiknya (περίστικτον φολίδεσσι).
claims.quote: δήεις κεγχρίνεω δολιχὸν τέρας, ὅν τε λέοντα αἰόλον αὐδάξαντο, περίστικτον φολίδεσσι

claims.statement: When the sun's (ἠελίοιο) ray is hottest it rages over the jagged mountains (οὔρεα), craving blood (αἵματος) and lying in wait for tame sheep (μῆλα).
claims.statement_id: Ketika sinar matahari (ἠελίοιο) paling terik, ia mengamuk menjelajahi gunung-gunung berbatu (οὔρεα), haus darah (αἵματος), dan mengintai domba jinak (μῆλα).
claims.quote: Ἤτοι ὅτ’ ἠελίοιο θερειτάτη ἵσταται ἀκτὶς, οὔρεα μαιμώσσων ἐπινίσσεται ὀκριόεντα, αἵματος ἰσχανόων, καὶ ἐπὶ κτίλα μῆλα δοκεύων

claims.statement: Nicander names Saos (Σάου) and Mosychlos (Μοσύχλου), where the flocks of the fields cool off under tall firs (ἐλάτῃσι) when the herdsmen (νομήων) have left their work.
claims.statement_id: Nikandros menyebut gunung Saos (Σάου) dan Mosychlos (Μοσύχλου), tempat kawanan di padang berteduh di bawah pohon cemara tinggi (ἐλάτῃσι) setelah para penggembala (νομήων) meninggalkan pekerjaan mereka.
claims.quote: ἢ Σάου ἠὲ Μοσύχλου ὅτ’ ἀμφ’ ἐλάτῃσι μακεδναῖς ἄγραυλοι ψύχωσι, λελοιπότες ἔργα νομήων

claims.statement: Nicander advises fleeing (Φεῦγε) by a winding, not a single straight path, because in many-turning bends its spine (ἀκάνθης) is hampered, while on a straight track it crawls very swiftly (ὢκιστος).
claims.statement_id: Nikandros menasihati agar orang melarikan diri (Φεῦγε) melalui jalur yang berkelok-kelok dan tidak lurus, karena di tikungan yang berliku tulang punggungnya (ἀκάνθης) terhambat, sedangkan di jalur lurus ia merayap sangat cepat (ὢκιστος).
claims.quote: Φεῦγε δ’ ἀεὶ σκολιήν τε καὶ οὐ μίαν ἀτραπὸν ἴλλων. δοχμὸς ἀνακρούων θηρὸς πάτον· ἦ γὰρ ὃ δεσμοὺς βλάπτεται ἐν καμπῇσι πολυστρέπτοισιν ἀκάνθης, ἰθεῖαν δ’ ὢκιστος ἐπιδρομάδην στίβον ἕρπει.

claims.statement: Such a snake (ὄφις) haunts the Thracian islands (Θρηικίῃσιν νήσοισι).
claims.statement_id: Ular (ὄφις) seperti itu berkeliaran di pulau-pulau Thrakia (Θρηικίῃσιν νήσοισι).
claims.quote: Τοῖος Θρηικίῃσιν ὄφις νήσοισι πολάζει.

claims.statement: Kwammanga is a special figure of San (Bushman) mythology: neither human nor animal, but part of the rainbow and living in it.
claims.statement_id: Kwammanga adalah tokoh khusus dalam mitologi orang San (Bushmen): bukan manusia, bukan hewan, melainkan bagian dari pelangi dan tinggal di dalamnya.
claims.quote: Куаманга (Kwammanga) е особен персонаж в бушменската митология. Той е този, който не е нито човек, нито животно, а е част от дъгата и живее в нея.

claims.statement: For the San he symbolises consciousness and thought and the critical side of human character; he is also responsible for ensuring that a flood never happens again.
claims.statement_id: Bagi orang San ia melambangkan kesadaran dan pikiran serta sisi kritis watak manusia; ia juga bertanggung jawab agar banjir besar tidak pernah terjadi lagi.
claims.quote: Той е символ на съзнанието и мисълта при бушмените, както и на критическия аспект в човешкия характер. Отговорен е и за това никога повече да не се случва потоп.

claims.statement: He is married to Tso, a porcupine, adopted daughter of the creator god Cagn and natural daughter of the fearsome devourer god Kwai-Hemm.
claims.statement_id: Ia menikah dengan Tso, seekor landak, anak angkat dewa pencipta Cagn dan anak kandung dewa pelahap yang menakutkan, Kwai-Hemm.
claims.quote: Женен е за Цо – бодливо свинче, осиновена дъщеря на бога-създател Цагн и родна дъщеря на страховития бог-поглъщач Кваи-Хему.

claims.statement: Kwammanga and Tso have two sons; the elder, Ni, is an Egyptian mongoose (ichneumon) and in many myths a partner of Cagn.
claims.statement_id: Kwammanga dan Tso punya dua putra; yang sulung, Ni, adalah garangan Mesir (ichneumon) dan dalam banyak mitos menjadi rekan Cagn.
claims.quote: Куаманга и Цо имат двама сина. По-големият Ни е египетска мангуста (ихневмон) и в много митове е партньор на Цагн.

claims.statement: The younger, named after his father Kwammanga, is also a rainbow and is kind, carefree and gentle in soul and body.
claims.statement_id: Putra bungsu, yang bernama sama dengan ayahnya, Kwammanga, juga berupa pelangi dan bersifat ramah, riang, berjiwa dan bertubuh lembut.
claims.quote: По-малкият, който носи името на баща си Куаманга, също е дъга и е мил, безгрижен, с нежна душа и тяло.

claims.statement: In the myth of the killing of the antelope, one year drought struck the San lands; for a long time not a drop of rain fell, and the earth dried and cracked.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos pembunuhan antelop, suatu tahun kemarau melanda tanah orang San; lama tak turun setetes hujan, dan tanah mengering serta retak.
claims.quote: Една година суша застигнала земите на бушмените, много време не паднала и капчица дъжд, земята изсъхнала и се напукала.

claims.statement: The two Kwammangas, father and son, knew they would be punished if they killed the old antelope, but hunger forced them to do it.
claims.statement_id: Kedua Kwammanga, ayah dan anak, tahu bahwa mereka akan dihukum bila membunuh antelop tua itu, tetapi rasa lapar memaksa mereka melakukannya.
claims.quote: Те знаели, че ако я убият ще бъдат наказани, но гладът ги принудил да го направят.

claims.statement: The people ate it without remorse for destroying another living being created by God, but guilt then lodged in their minds like a scourge and began to torment them.
claims.statement_id: Orang-orang memakannya tanpa menyesal telah membinasakan makhluk hidup ciptaan Tuhan, tetapi rasa bersalah lalu bersarang di benak mereka dan menyiksa mereka.
claims.quote: Хората я изяли без да почувстват угризение за това, че унищожават друго живо същество, сътворено от Бога. Но вината се загнездила като бич в съзнанието им и започнала да ги мъчи.

claims.statement: They had to turn for help to the creator god Cagn, because they could no longer live with such great guilt.
claims.statement_id: Mereka terpaksa meminta pertolongan kepada dewa pencipta Cagn karena tak sanggup lagi hidup dengan rasa bersalah yang begitu besar.
claims.quote: се наложило да се обърнат за помощ към бога-творец Цагн, защото повече не можели да живеят с тази огромна вина.

claims.statement: The Porcupine is married to Kwammang-a, a mythical person not identified with any animal but seen in the rainbow.
claims.statement_id: Si Landak (Porcupine) menikah dengan Kwammang-a, tokoh mitis yang tidak disamakan dengan hewan apa pun, tetapi terlihat dalam pelangi (rainbow).
claims.quote: The Porcupine is married to Kwammang-a*, a mythical person not identified with any animal, but seen in the rainbow.

claims.statement: The couple have two children: young Kwammang-a, brave and quiet like his father, and the young Ichneumon, a great talker always lecturing his grandfather the Mantis.
claims.statement_id: Pasangan itu punya dua anak: Kwammang-a muda, pemberani dan pendiam seperti ayahnya, dan Ichneumon muda yang banyak bicara dan selalu menasihati kakeknya, si Mantis (Mantis).
claims.quote: This strange couple have two children, young Kwammang-a, who is brave and quiet like his father, and the young Ichneumon, who is a great talker, always lecturing his grandfather the Mantis on his foolish doings.

claims.statement: In one tale the Mantis calls Kwammang-a "my sister's son".
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah, si Mantis menyebut Kwammang-a "anak saudara perempuanku".
claims.quote: In one tale the Mantis calls him ‘‘ my sister’s son.”

claims.statement: The Mantis made an Eland out of Kwammang-a's shoe.
claims.statement_id: Si Mantis membuat seekor eland (Eland) dari sepatu Kwammang-a.
claims.quote: Then the Mantis made an Eland out of Kwammang-a's shoe.

claims.statement: The Rainbow is yellow above and red below, because the Mantis, who is also yellow, lies above and Kwammang-a lies below.
claims.statement_id: Pelangi (Rainbow) kuning di bagian atas dan merah di bagian bawah, karena si Mantis yang juga kuning berada di atas, sedangkan Kwammang-a berada di bawah.
claims.quote: The Rainbow is yellow in that part which lies above ; the piece which seems red lies below. For the Mantis, who 1s also yellow, lies above, and Kwammang-a lies below.

claims.statement: The Rainbow is called Kwammang-a; children call it so because the grown-up people called it so.
claims.statement_id: Pelangi (Rainbow) itu disebut Kwammang-a; anak-anak menyebutnya begitu karena orang dewasa menyebutnya demikian.
claims.quote: It is the Rainbow. Men call it Kwammang-a. Therefore we who are children say ‘* Kwammang-a "to it, because the grown-up people said Kwammang-a to it.

claims.statement: People say: "The Rainbow stands yonder and the rain will break."
claims.statement_id: Orang berkata: "Pelangi (Rainbow) berdiri di sana dan hujan akan reda."
claims.quote: The Rainbow stands yonder and the rain will break.

claims.statement: In Bulgarian folk belief Kutsulan is the name of the most dangerous and bloodthirsty wolf; though usually a lone wolf, he is regarded as leader of the wolf pack.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Bulgaria, Kutsulan adalah nama serigala yang paling berbahaya dan haus darah; meski biasanya serigala penyendiri, ia dianggap pemimpin kawanan serigala.
claims.quote: в българските народни вярвания е името на най-опасния и кръвожаден вълк. Въпреки че това обикновено е вълкът-единак, той е приеман като водач на вълчата глутница.

claims.statement: He is pictured as a big lame wolf, but sometimes as an old man, and is given the role of shepherd of the wolves.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai serigala besar yang pincang, tetapi kadang sebagai lelaki tua, dan diberi peran sebagai penggembala para serigala.
claims.quote: Представян е като голям куц вълк, но понякога и като стар човек и му се отрежда ролята на пастир на вълците.

claims.statement: According to belief, God once gave the wolves time to eat; all the wolves seized some prey except one lame wolf, who did not arrive in time and stayed hungry.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan, dahulu Tuhan memberi waktu kepada para serigala untuk makan; semua serigala mendapat mangsa, kecuali seekor serigala pincang yang tidak tiba tepat waktu dan tetap lapar.
claims.quote: Според поверието някога Господ дал време на вълците да ядат. Всички вълци успели да грабнат някакво животно за плячка, само един куц вълк не успял да стигне навреме и останал гладен.

claims.statement: He stopped under a tree where a man was picking fruit and wanted to eat him; the man replied that this was not right, and they asked God to decide.
claims.statement_id: Ia berhenti di bawah pohon tempat seorang lelaki memetik buah dan ingin memakannya; lelaki itu menjawab bahwa itu tidak benar, lalu keduanya meminta keputusan Tuhan.
claims.quote: Спрял под едно дърво, на което имало човек, берящ плодове и поискал да го изяде. Човекът отвърнал, че това не е правилно и се допитали до Бог.

claims.statement: After hearing them, God ruled that the wolf might eat the man, which the wolf did.
claims.statement_id: Setelah mendengarkan keduanya, Tuhan memutuskan bahwa serigala boleh memakan manusia itu, dan serigala pun melakukannya.
claims.quote: Господ след като ги изслушал отсъдил, че вълкът може да изяде човека, което вълкът и сторил.

claims.statement: Since then this wolf (Kutsulan) has been the most dangerous to people and animals.
claims.statement_id: Sejak itu serigala ini (Kutsulan) menjadi yang paling berbahaya bagi manusia dan hewan.
claims.quote: Оттогава този вълк (Куцулан) е най-опасният за хората и животните.

claims.statement: Kutsulan is also the name of the last day of the Wolf Holidays (Valchi praznitsi).
claims.statement_id: Kutsulan juga nama hari terakhir dari Hari Raya Serigala (Valchi praznitsi).
claims.quote: Куцулан се нарича също и последният ден от Вълчите празници.

claims.statement: In the imagination of the Bulgarians (българите) this lone wolf is the mythical leader of the pack, described as lame or one-legged (compare the lame devil), and called Kutsulan (Куцулан), Klekutsan (Клекуцан), Natlapan (Натлапан) or Krivlyo (Кривльо).
claims.statement_id: Dalam bayangan orang Bulgaria (българите), serigala penyendiri ini adalah pemimpin mitis kawanan, digambarkan pincang atau berkaki satu (bandingkan iblis pincang), dan disebut Kutsulan (Куцулан), Klekutsan (Клекуцан), Natlapan (Натлапан), atau Krivlyo (Кривльо).
claims.quote: В представите на българите това е митичният предводител на глутницата, описван е като куц или еднокрак (срв. с куция дявол) и е наричан Куцулан, Клекуцан, Натлапан или Кривльо.

claims.statement: Lehusa, also leusa or levusa (Greek: Eleousa), is a Bulgarian dialect term for a woman who has just given birth.
claims.statement_id: Lehusa, juga leusa atau levusa (bahasa Yunani: Eleousa), adalah sebutan dialek Bulgaria untuk perempuan yang baru melahirkan.
claims.quote: Лехуса, още леуса или левуса (на гръцки: Ελεούσα, Елеуса), е българско диалектно название на родилката.

claims.statement: It comes from the Greek word eleousa, meaning "merciful", often used to name the Most Holy Mother of God.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini berasal dari kata Yunani eleousa yang berarti "yang penuh belas kasih", sebutan yang sering dipakai untuk Bunda Maria.
claims.quote: Произлиза от гръцката дума елеуса, в превод милостива, с която често се назовава Пресвета Богородица.

claims.statement: According to Bulgarian folk belief, lehusi are also spirits that visit new mothers until the 40th day after birth; if not stopped, they bring illness, madness and death.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Bulgaria, lehusa juga roh-roh yang mendatangi ibu yang baru melahirkan hingga hari ke-40 setelah persalinan; jika tidak dicegah, mereka membawa penyakit, kegilaan, dan kematian.
claims.quote: Според българските народни вярвания лехусите са и духове, които идват при родилките до 40-ия ден след раждането. Ако не бъдат спрени, донасят болести, лудост, смърт.

claims.statement: Therefore someone must always be with the mother and baby until that day, and after the 40th day a honey loaf is kneaded to appease the spirits.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu, ibu dan bayi harus selalu ditemani seseorang sampai hari itu, dan setelah hari ke-40 berlalu dibuatlah roti madu untuk menenangkan para roh.
claims.quote: Затова при майката и бебето до този ден винаги трябва да има някого, а след изтичане на 40тия ден се омесва медена пита, за да ги умилостиви.

claims.statement: The sequel to the audio series "Мамник" (Mamnik) was released on Storytel under the title "Лехуса" (Lehusa), again voiced by Vlado Penev (Владо Пенев).
claims.statement_id: Lanjutan serial audio "Мамник" (Mamnik) dirilis di Storytel dengan judul "Лехуса" (Lehusa) dan kembali dibacakan oleh Vlado Penev (Владо Пенев).
claims.quote: Дългоочакваното продължение на хитовия аудиосериал “Мамник” излезе тази седмица в Storytel. Новата част носи заглавието “Лехуса” и отново е озвучена от незабравимия глас на Владо Пенев.

claims.statement: According to the author Vasil Popov (Васил Попов), the lehusa is a creature of Bulgarian tradition, a kind of spirit or monster born of the pain of a woman whose child was taken from her by force, and is believed to pursue new mothers and pregnant women.
claims.statement_id: Menurut pengarang Vasil Popov (Васил Попов), lehusa adalah makhluk dari tradisi Bulgaria, semacam roh atau monster yang lahir dari derita seorang perempuan yang anaknya direnggut paksa, dan dipercaya memburu perempuan yang baru melahirkan dan perempuan hamil.
claims.quote: Лехусата е създание от нашата традиция – нещо като дух или чудовище, родено от болката на жена, на която насилствено са отнели детето. Вярва се, че преследва родилки и бременни”, обяснява авторът Васил Попов

claims.statement: In Bulgarian folk belief Mratinyak is a malevolent demon causing the disease of the same name in hens and poultry (also called hen disease), the personification of poultry diseases.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Bulgaria, Mratinyak adalah demon jahat yang menyebabkan penyakit bernama sama pada ayam dan unggas (disebut juga penyakit ayam), personifikasi penyakit unggas.
claims.quote: в българските народни вярвания е злотворен демон, причиняващ едноименната болест по кокошките и домашните птици (наричана още кокоша болест), олицетворение на болестите по домашните птици.

claims.statement: Mainly in Northern and Western Bulgaria the feast of Mratintsi is kept in his honour; he is pictured as a big, extremely ugly black hen with large wings and huge eyes.
claims.statement_id: Terutama di Bulgaria Utara dan Barat dirayakan hari raya Mratintsi untuk menghormatinya; ia digambarkan sebagai ayam betina hitam besar yang sangat buruk rupa, bersayap besar dan bermata sangat besar.
claims.quote: Главно в Северна и Западна България в негова чест се почита празника Мратинци. Представян е като голяма черна кокошка с изключително грозен вид, големи криле и огромни очи.

claims.statement: The Mratintsi custom is known mainly in Northern and Western Bulgaria (България) and is kept on 14 November, the day of the Apostle Philip (Филип) in the Orthodox calendar, traditionally linked with the start of the Christmas fast and the end of the wedding season.
claims.statement_id: Adat Mratintsi dikenal terutama di Bulgaria Utara dan Barat (България) dan dirayakan pada 14 November, hari Rasul Filipus (Филип) dalam kalender Ortodoks, yang secara tradisional dikaitkan dengan awal puasa Natal dan akhir musim pernikahan.
claims.quote: Известен е главно в Северна и Западна България и се чества на 14 ноември (в православния календар това е денят на апостол Филип, свързван традиционно с началото на Коледните пости и с края на сватбения сезон).

claims.statement: In some places in Western Bulgaria, Mratintsi denotes the period of 11–16 (21) November, a local variant of the Wolf Holidays (Вълчите празници).
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa tempat di Bulgaria Barat, Mratintsi menandai periode 11–16 (21) November, sebagai varian lokal Hari Raya Serigala (Вълчите празници).
claims.quote: На някои места в Западна България с Мратинци се обозначава периодът 11 – 16 (21) ноември, явяващ се местен вариант на Вълчите празници.

claims.statement: The Mratintsi nights were considered more dangerous even than the Mrasnite dni (Мръсните дни), the time when, in old belief, the most dangerous and disease-bringing evil forces run wild.
claims.statement_id: Malam-malam Mratintsi dianggap lebih berbahaya bahkan daripada Mrasnite dni (Мръсните дни), masa ketika menurut bayangan lama kekuatan jahat yang paling berbahaya dan pembawa penyakit merajalela.
claims.quote: Мратинските нощи са считани за по-опасни дори и от Мръсните дни (и нощи) - време, в което, в старинните представи, вилнеят най-опасните и болестотворни зли сили

claims.statement: The ritual is performed by women: to appease the mratinyak (мратиняка), on that day they slaughter a chicken, usually a young cockerel, preferably a black one.
claims.statement_id: Ritualnya dilakukan oleh perempuan: untuk meredakan mratinyak (мратиняка), pada hari itu mereka menyembelih seekor anak ayam, biasanya jantan, sebaiknya yang hitam.
claims.quote: Ритуалът се изпълнява от жени. За да умилостивят мратиняка, на този ден колят пиле (обикновено - петле, т.е. мъжко дете на кокошка), за предпочитане - черно.

claims.statement: When the older woman puts the knife to the chicken's neck, the younger asks "What are you slaughtering?"; the older answers "I am slaughtering mratinyak (мратиняк)" and kills it, saying "It is not we who slaughter you, it is mratinyak who slaughters you."
claims.statement_id: Saat perempuan tua menempelkan pisau ke leher ayam, perempuan yang lebih muda bertanya "Apa yang kau sembelih?"; yang tua menjawab "Aku menyembelih mratinyak (мратиняк)", lalu menyembelihnya sambil berkata "Bukan kami yang menyembelihmu, mratinyak yang menyembelihmu."
claims.quote: Когато възрастната опре ножа до врата на пилето, по-младата пита: „Какво колиш?“, на което по-възрастната отговаря: „Коля мратиняк.“ и заколва пилето, отправяйки му следната реплика: „Не те колим ние, но те коли мратиняк.“

claims.statement: The chicken is cooked and eaten, while its feathers are kept and burned when needed to treat various illnesses by fumigation (прекадяване).
claims.statement_id: Ayam itu dimasak dan dimakan, sedangkan bulunya disimpan dan bila perlu dibakar untuk mengobati berbagai penyakit dengan pengasapan (прекадяване).
claims.quote: Пилето се сготвя и изяжда, а перушината се запазва и при случай перата се горят за лекуване (чрез прекадяване с дим) на разни болести.

claims.statement: In some parts of the Balkans there was a belief in an unusual creature called the service spirit or house spirit.
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa daerah Balkan ada kepercayaan tentang makhluk aneh yang disebut roh pelayan atau roh rumah.
claims.quote: У неким крајевима Балкана постојало је веровање у необично створење које се називало услужни или кућни дух.

claims.statement: In some places this spirit was also called malić, macić, domaći, škrat, and elsewhere špiritus.
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa tempat roh ini juga disebut malić, macić, domaći, škrat, dan di tempat lain špiritus.
claims.quote: Негде се овај дух звао и малић, мацић, домаћи, шкрат, а понегде шпиритус.

claims.statement: Other peoples also know the service spirit: in Germany it is called kobold, in England good fellow, in Sweden spirit, and in Russia domovoi.
claims.statement_id: Bangsa lain juga mengenal roh pelayan: di Jerman disebut kobold, di Inggris good fellow, di Swedia spirit, dan di Rusia domovoi.
claims.quote: И други народи знају за услужног духа. У Немачкој га називају коболд, у Енглеској гуд фелоу, Шведској спирит, а у Русији домовој.

claims.statement: The service spirit is very small; some say it is the size of a thumb, others that it can grow to the height of a small child.
claims.statement_id: Roh pelayan bertubuh sangat kecil; ada yang menyebutnya sebesar ibu jari, ada pula yang menyebut ia bisa tumbuh setinggi anak kecil.
claims.quote: Услужни дух је сасвим малог раста. Негде кажу да је величине палца, а негде да може да нарасте до висине малог детета.

claims.statement: It wears čakšire trousers and always has a little red cap on its head.
claims.statement_id: Ia mengenakan celana čakšire dan selalu memakai topi kecil merah di kepalanya.
claims.quote: Обучен је у чакшире, а на глави обавезно носи црвену капицу.

claims.statement: It most often lives in the chimney, under the table or under some vessel in the kitchen.
claims.statement_id: Ia paling sering tinggal di cerobong, di bawah meja, atau di bawah perkakas di dapur.
claims.quote: Најчешће обитава у оџаку, под столом или испод каквог суда и кухињи.

claims.statement: Formerly various magic was bought at apothecaries, so in some places a service spirit could also be bought, neatly packed in a bottle.
claims.statement_id: Dahulu berbagai sihir dibeli di apotek, sehingga di beberapa tempat roh pelayan juga bisa dibeli, dikemas rapi dalam botol.
claims.quote: Наиме некада су се разне магије куповале у апотекама, па је тако понегде могао да се купи и услужни дух, и то уредно спакован у флаши.

claims.statement: Another way was to obtain an egg laid by a nine-year-old cock or by a hen that had begun to crow.
claims.statement_id: Cara lain adalah mendapatkan telur yang dierami oleh ayam jantan berumur sembilan tahun atau oleh ayam betina yang mulai berkokok.
claims.quote: Требало се само домоћи јајета које је снео деветогодишњи петао или кокошка која је почела да кукуриче.

claims.statement: Such an egg had to be carried under the left armpit for forty days, sitting behind the stove, without cutting one's hair or shaving.
claims.statement_id: Telur itu harus dibawa di bawah ketiak kiri selama empat puluh hari, sambil duduk di belakang tungku, tanpa mencukur rambut dan janggut.
claims.quote: Такво јаје човек је морао да носи под левим пазухом четрдесет дана, да седи иза пећи, не шиша се и не брије.

claims.statement: This house dwarf could fulfil every wish of its master, do him all kinds of services and create whatever he imagined.
claims.statement_id: Kurcaci rumah ini mampu memenuhi setiap keinginan tuannya, memberinya berbagai layanan, dan menciptakan apa pun yang dibayangkan tuannya.
claims.quote: Овај кућни патуљак био је у стању да испуни сваку жељу свом господару, чини му разне услуге и створи све што би овај замислио.

claims.statement: If the owner neglected the house spirit, it would turn against him, changing from friend and benefactor into a dangerous, wicked enemy seeking to ruin its former owner in every way.
claims.statement_id: Jika pemiliknya lalai, roh rumah akan berbalik melawannya, berubah dari sahabat dan penolong menjadi musuh berbahaya dan jahat yang berusaha mencelakakan bekas pemiliknya dengan segala cara.
claims.quote: Уколико би власник био нехајан према кућном духу, он би се одметнуо од њега. Тада би се од пријатеља и доброчинитеља преобразио у опасног и опаког непријатеља који је гледао да свог бившег власника на сваки начин упропасти.

claims.statement: The only way to destroy it was to plunge it into boiling oil, which was not at all easy.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya cara memusnahkannya adalah menenggelamkannya dalam minyak mendidih, yang sama sekali tidak mudah.
claims.quote: Једини начин да се уништи био је да се потопи у врело уље, што није било нимало лако.

claims.statement: In Belarusian mythology the valatouny are giant maidens (volaty) of superhuman strength.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Belarus, valatouny adalah gadis-gadis raksasa (volat) berkekuatan adimanusiawi.
claims.quote: Валатоўны — у беларускай міфалогіі дзяўчаты-волаты са звышчалавечай сілай.

claims.statement: Many places in Belarus are linked with the valatouny: Darotsina hill (Drysa district), Bahatyr hill (Rasony district) and Dziavochaya hill (Mstsislau and Valozhyn districts).
claims.statement_id: Banyak tempat di Belarus dikaitkan dengan valatouny: bukit Darotsina (distrik Drysa), bukit Bahatyr (distrik Rasony), dan bukit Dziavochaya (distrik Mstsislau dan Valozhyn).
claims.quote: З персанажамі валатовен у Беларусі звязаны многія геаграфічныя аб’екты: Дароціна гара (Дрысенскі р-н), гара Багатыр (Расонскі р-н), Дзявочая гара (Мсціслаўскі, Валожынскі р-н).

claims.statement: Darota is a giant maiden who lived on the height now called Darotsina hill; she tossed logs back and forth with a giant maiden from Piarun hill, and fought an enemy army but died.
claims.statement_id: Darota adalah gadis raksasa yang tinggal di bukit yang kini disebut bukit Darotsina; ia saling melempar batang kayu dengan gadis raksasa dari bukit Piarun, dan bertempur melawan pasukan musuh hingga gugur.
claims.quote: Дарота — дзяўчына-волат, жыла на ўзвышшы, якое зараз завецца Дароцінай гарой. Перакідвалася бярвеннямі з дзяўчынай-волатам з Пярунавай гары. Змагаецца з варожым войскам, але гіне.

claims.statement: The valatouna of Bahatyr hill went every morning 10 versts for water and carried it in tubs each holding 30 buckets.
claims.statement_id: Valatouna dari bukit Bahatyr setiap pagi mengambil air sejauh 10 versta dan membawanya dalam ember-ember yang masing-masing memuat 30 ember biasa.
claims.quote: Кожную раніцу хадзіла па ваду за 10 вёрст і насіла яе цэбрамі, у кожным з якіх памясцілася б па 30 вёдзер.

claims.statement: The Tatars saw Saint Sophia of Polotsk from the top of Bahatyr hill and fell upon the valatouna; she struck down almost all of them with her yoke but died herself, and the water from her tubs flowed out to form the Bahatyrka river.
claims.statement_id: Orang Tatar melihat Katedral Santa Sofia Polotsk dari puncak bukit Bahatyr lalu menyerang valatouna; ia menewaskan hampir semuanya dengan pikulannya tetapi ikut gugur, dan air dari embernya mengalir membentuk Sungai Bahatyrka.
claims.quote: Між тым татары ўбачылі з вяршыні Багатыр-гары Святую Полацкую Сафію і накінуліся на валатоўну. Яна перабіла каромыслам амаль усіх, але і сама загінула. З цэбраў пацякла вада, ад якой утварылася рэчка Багатырка.

claims.statement: Hollows in boulders were often explained as footprints of the ancient giant maidens.
claims.statement_id: Cekungan pada batu-batu besar sering dijelaskan sebagai jejak kaki gadis-gadis raksasa zaman dahulu.
claims.quote: Паглыбленні на валунах нярэдка тлумачылі як водціскі ад ног старажытных дзяўчат-вяліканак.

claims.statement: According to E. Zaikouski, the ancient cult of the valatouny resembled that of the Mother Goddess; yet most tales link the giant maidens not with creative power (fertility) but with destruction, war and death.
claims.statement_id: Menurut E. Zaikouski, pemujaan kuno valatouny mirip pemujaan Dewi Ibu; namun sebagian besar kisah mengaitkan gadis raksasa ini bukan dengan daya cipta (kesuburan), melainkan dengan kehancuran, perang, dan kematian.
claims.quote: Як лічыць Э. Зайкоўскі, старажытны культ валатовен быў падобны да культу Багіні-Маці. Большасць сюжэтаў, аднак, звязвае дзяўчат-вяліканак не з творчай сілай (урадлівасць, плоднасць), а з разбурэннем, вайной і смерцю.

claims.statement: They may correspond to the Celtic goddess Morrígan and the Scandinavian warrior maidens, the valkyries.
claims.statement_id: Padanan mereka mungkin dewi Kelt Morrígan dan para valkyrie, gadis pejuang Skandinavia.
claims.quote: Ім можа адпавядаць кельцкая багіня Морыган і скандынаўскія ваяўнічыя дзевы-валькірыі.

claims.statement: In another legend the giant maiden Katsiaryna is wooed by 2 giants, Stsiapan and Marka, and promises to marry whoever throws a boulder farther.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda lain, gadis raksasa Katsiaryna dilamar oleh 2 raksasa, Stsiapan dan Marka, dan berjanji menikahi yang melempar batu besar paling jauh.
claims.quote: У другім паданні за Кацярыну сватаюцца 2 волаты — Сцяпан і Марка. Дзяўчына-волат абяцае выйсці за таго, хто кіне валун далей.

claims.statement: Marka, whom she did not love, won; to escape marrying him Katsiaryna threw herself from the boulder, turned into water that vanished into the earth and came out as a spring 5 versts from Prapoisk, called "Sini kalodzezh" (the Blue Well).
claims.statement_id: Marka yang tidak dicintainya menang; untuk menghindari pernikahan, Katsiaryna melompat dari batu, berubah menjadi air yang lenyap ke tanah dan muncul sebagai mata air 5 versta dari Prapoisk, yang dinamai "Sini kalodzezh" (Sumur Biru).
claims.quote: Перамагае нялюбы ёй Марка, і Кацярына, каб пазбегнуць шлюбу з ім, кідаецца з валуна, разлілася вадою, якая знікла ў зямлі і выйшла на свет крыніцай за 5 вёрст ад Прапойска. Тую крыніцу празвалі «Сіні калодзеж».

claims.statement: In Belarusian mythology Vetser (the Wind) is a personified natural phenomenon, described as an ugly fat man with a mouth like a goose's beak.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Belarus, Vetser (Angin) adalah gejala alam yang dipersonifikasikan, digambarkan sebagai lelaki gemuk buruk rupa dengan mulut seperti paruh angsa.
claims.quote: Вецер - у беларускай міфалогіі персаніфікаваная прыродная з'ява. Апісваўся як пачварны тоўсты чалавек з ротам, падобным да гусінай дзюбы.

claims.statement: To raise a strong wind he opens his beak wide, and for a cold wind he presses it tight, leaving a small opening at the tip.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menimbulkan angin kencang ia membuka lebar paruhnya, dan untuk angin dingin ia merapatkannya dan menyisakan lubang kecil di ujungnya.
claims.quote: Каб выклікаць моцны вецер, ён шырока раскрывае сваю дзюбу, а каб халодны - шчыльна сцісквае і пакідае на канцы невялічную адтуліну.

claims.statement: Belarusians believed that millers (generally considered sorcerers by the people) had to be able to "harness the wind", summoning it when needed.
claims.statement_id: Orang Belarus percaya bahwa tukang giling (yang umumnya dianggap tukang sihir oleh rakyat) harus mampu "memasang kekang pada angin", memanggilnya pada saat dibutuhkan.
claims.quote: Беларусы верылі, што млынары (якія наогул лічыліся ў народзе чараўнікамі) павінны ўмець "запрагаць вецер", выклікаць яго ў патрэбны час.

claims.statement: Zhyzhal (also Zhyzh, Zhyzha, Zhyzhak) is an ancient Belarusian fire god proposed by the folklorist Pavel Shpilevsky.
claims.statement_id: Zhyzhal (juga Zhyzh, Zhyzha, Zhyzhak) adalah dewa api Belarus kuno yang diajukan oleh folkloris Pavel Shpilevsky.
claims.quote: (Жыж, Жыжа, Жыжак) — прапанаваны фалькларыстам Паўлам Шпілеўскім старажытнабеларускі бог агню.

claims.statement: The spirit Zhyzhal was supposedly believed in mainly in Minsk Governorate; in Belarusian conception Zhyzhal lives underground and releases fire from himself there.
claims.statement_id: Roh Zhyzhal konon dipercaya terutama di wilayah Kegubernuran Minsk; menurut gambaran orang Belarus, Zhyzhal tinggal di bawah tanah dan di sana mengeluarkan api dari dirinya.
claims.quote: У духа Жыжаля нібыта верылі ў асноўным на тэрыторыі Мінскай губерні. Паводле ўяўленняў беларусаў Жыжаль жыве пад зямлёй і там выпускае з сябе агонь.

claims.statement: When he does this slowly the earth warms; when quickly, fires break out on the surface, meadows and forests perish, and fields and gardens dry up and become barren.
claims.statement_id: Jika ia melakukannya perlahan, bumi menjadi hangat; jika cepat, timbul kebakaran di permukaan bumi, padang rumput dan hutan musnah, ladang dan kebun mengering hingga menjadi tandus.
claims.quote: Калі ён робіць гэта павольна, то зямля саграваецца, а калі хутка, то ўзнікаюць на зямной паверхні пажары, гінуць сенажаці і лясы, высушваюцца палі і агароды, ад чаго яны робяцца бясплоднымі.

claims.statement: There was a saying "Zhyzh has taken to coming", meaning "drought or fire has begun to occur often".
claims.statement_id: Ada ungkapan "Zhyzh sudah terbiasa datang", yang berarti "kekeringan atau kebakaran mulai sering terjadi".
claims.quote: Існавалі выслоўі: «Жыж унадзіўся», г. зн. «сталі часта ўзнікаць засуха ці пажар»

claims.statement: P. Shpilevsky derived the deity from proverbs and from the children's word for fire, "zhyzha".
claims.statement_id: P. Shpilevsky menurunkan dewa ini dari peribahasa dan dari kata kanak-kanak untuk api, "zhyzha".
claims.quote: П. Шпілеўскі вывеў боства з прымавак і дзіцячай назвы агню «жыжа».

claims.statement: He is mentioned among the enemies of Perun.

claims.quote: Узгадваецца сярод ворагаў Пяруна.

claims.statement: The annual Belarusian art festival of ceramists and potters, "Art-Zhyzhal", is named in honour of Zhyzhal; in summer 2015 it was held for the 13th time.
claims.statement_id: Festival seni tahunan Belarus untuk perajin keramik dan tembikar, "Art-Zhyzhal", dinamai untuk menghormati Zhyzhal; pada musim panas 2015 festival itu sudah diadakan untuk ke-13 kalinya.
claims.quote: У гонар Жыжаля названы штогадовы беларускі мастацкі фестываль керамістаў і ганчароў «Арт-Жыжаль», які летам 2015 года праводзіўся ўжо ў 13 раз.

claims.statement: In Belarusian mythology Kingi is a beautiful queen whose palace stood by the Narew river, not far from where it flows into the Bug.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Belarus, Kingi adalah ratu jelita yang istananya berdiri di tepi Sungai Narew, tidak jauh dari muaranya ke Sungai Bug.
claims.quote: Кінгі — у беларускай міфалогіі прыгажуня-каралева, палац якой стаяў ля ракі Нараў, недалёка ад месца ўпадзення ў Буг.

claims.statement: As the beauty walked in her garden listening to birdsong, the earth suddenly shook, the palace sank down and a small hill rose in its place.
claims.statement_id: Ketika sang ratu berjalan-jalan di tamannya sambil mendengarkan kicau burung, bumi tiba-tiba berguncang, istananya amblas, dan di tempatnya tumbuh sebuah bukit kecil.
claims.quote: Калі прыгажуня гуляла па сваім садзе і слухала спевы птушак, зямля раптам затрэслася, і палац праваліўся ўніз, а на яго месцы вырасла невялічкая гара.

claims.statement: Since then Kingi came out of the earth every night and lit a bonfire, waiting for someone to pick flowers for her; but people who saw the fire from afar avoided the suspicious place.
claims.statement_id: Sejak itu Kingi setiap malam keluar dari tanah dan menyalakan api unggun, menunggu seseorang memetikkan bunga untuknya; tetapi orang yang melihat api itu dari jauh selalu menghindari tempat yang mencurigakan itu.
claims.quote: З таго часу Кінгі кожную ноч выходзіла з зямлі і раскладала вогнішча, чакаючы, пакуль хтосьці з людзей нарве ёй кветак. Але людзі, пабачыўшы вогнішча здалёку, абыходзілі падазронае месца бокам.

claims.statement: Once an old robber noticed the fire; Kingi offered him gold in exchange for flowers, but the robber attacked her with a knife, whereupon the maiden vanished and the thief turned into a boulder.
claims.statement_id: Suatu kali seorang perampok tua melihat api itu; Kingi menawarkan emas sebagai imbalan bunga, tetapi perampok itu menyerangnya dengan pisau, lalu sang gadis lenyap dan si pencuri berubah menjadi batu besar.
claims.quote: Аднойчы агонь заўважыў стары разбойнік. Кінгі прапанавала яму нарваць кветак у абмен на золата. Разбойнік кінуўся на яе з нажом, але дзяўчына знікла, а злодзей ператварыўся ў валун.

claims.statement: The legend combines several popular plots at once: settlements that sank into the earth, a man who turned to stone, and so on.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini menggabungkan beberapa alur populer sekaligus: permukiman yang amblas ke dalam tanah, manusia yang menjadi batu, dan sebagainya.
claims.quote: Легенда спалучае адразу некалькі папулярных сюжэтаў: пра паселішчы, якія праваліліся пад зямлю; пра чалавека, які стаў камнем і г.д.

claims.statement: Yashchar or Yashchur is a hypothetical pagan deity worshipped by the ancestors of modern Belarusians and by the Slavic population of northern Rus.
claims.statement_id: Yashchar atau Yashchur adalah dewa pagan hipotetis yang dipuja leluhur orang Belarus modern dan penduduk Slavia di Rus utara.
claims.quote: Яшчар або Яшчур — гіпатэтычнае язычніцкае боства, якому пакланяліся продкі сучасных беларусаў, а таксама славянскае насельніцтва паўночнай Русі.

claims.statement: According to A. L. Barkova, Yashchar is a serpent god, lord of the sea and underground waters, whose sanctuaries lay near marshes, lakes and rivers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut A. L. Barkova, Yashchar adalah dewa ular, penguasa laut dan air bawah tanah, dan tempat pemujaannya berada di dekat rawa, danau, dan sungai.
claims.quote: Паводле А. Л. Барковай, Яшчар — гэта бог-змей, уладар мора і падземных вод. Яго капішчы размяшчаліся ля балот, азёр і рэк.

claims.statement: Black hens and young girls were offered to Yashchar as sacrifices, which is reflected in many beliefs where a serpent (most often a grass snake) takes a girl and makes her his wife.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai kurban bagi Yashchar dipersembahkan ayam hitam dan gadis muda, yang tercermin dalam banyak takhayul ketika ular (biasanya ular air) mengambil seorang gadis dan menjadikannya istri.
claims.quote: У якасці ахвяр Яшчару прыносілі чорных кур і маладых дзяўчын, што адлюстравалася ў шматлікіх павер’ях, дзе змей (часцей за ўсё вуж) забірае сабе дзяўчыну і робіць сваёй жонкай.

claims.statement: Among Belarusian peasants a game of Yashchar was known, in which a youth or boy plays the character of that name and chooses a "bride".
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan petani Belarus dikenal permainan Yashchar, di mana seorang pemuda atau anak laki-laki memerankan tokoh itu dan memilih "pengantin" untuk dirinya.
claims.quote: вядома гульня ў Яшчара, дзе юнак ці хлопчык граюць ролю аднайменнага персанажа, выбіраюць сабе «нявесту».

claims.statement: In B. A. Rybakov's view the game may be a remnant of the idea of a serpent-like deity choosing a "wife", a girl to be sacrificed.
claims.statement_id: Menurut B. A. Rybakov, permainan ini mungkin sisa gagasan tentang dewa berwujud ular yang memilih "istri", yaitu gadis untuk dikurbankan.
claims.quote: На думку Б. А. Рыбакова гульня можа быць рэшткай уяўлення пра змеепадобнае боства, якое выбірае сабе «жонку» — дзяўчыну дзеля ахвярапрынашэння.

claims.statement: Since the thunder god of Indo-European peoples was often a serpent-slayer, the hypothesis of enmity between the ancient gods Perun and Yashchar is considered sound.
claims.statement_id: Karena dewa guntur bangsa-bangsa Indo-Eropa sering menjadi pembunuh ular, hipotesis tentang permusuhan antara dewa kuno Perun dan Yashchar dianggap beralasan.
claims.quote: Улічваючы тое, што грамавержац у індаеўрапейскіх народаў часта з’яўляўся змееборцам, мае рацыю гіпотэза аб ворагаванні старажытных багоў Пяруна і Яшчара.

claims.statement: According to A. L. Barkova, Yashchar was originally the chief deity of the Novgorodians until Vladimir (the future baptiser) imposed the cult of Perun on them.
claims.statement_id: Menurut A. L. Barkova, Yashchar awalnya dewa utama orang Novgorod sampai Vladimir (kelak pembaptis Rus) memaksakan pemujaan Perun kepada mereka.
claims.quote: Паводле А. Л. Барковай, Яшчар спачатку быў галоўным бозствам наўгародцаў, пакуль Уладзімір (будучы хрысціцель) не насадзіў ім культ Пяруна.

claims.statement: The svitsiazianki are mythical beings of Lake Svitsiaz in Karelichy district, a kind of rusalka.
claims.statement_id: Svitsiazianki adalah makhluk mitos Danau Svitsiaz di distrik Karelichy, sejenis rusalka.
claims.quote: міфічныя істоты возера Свіцязь у Карэліцкім раёне, адмена русалак.

claims.statement: Legends of the svitsiazianki, earthly women or girls transformed through tragic events, were widespread at Svitsiaz and up to 20-30 km around the lake.
claims.statement_id: Legenda tentang svitsiazianki, yaitu perempuan atau gadis duniawi yang berubah wujud karena peristiwa tragis, tersebar luas di Svitsiaz dan sekitarnya hingga 20-30 km dari danau.
claims.quote: Паданні пра свіцязянак, у якіх ператварыліся зямныя жанчыны або дзяўчаты праз пэўныя трагічныя падзеі, былі шырока распаўсюджаны на Свіцязі і ў ваколіцах за 20-30 км ад возера

claims.statement: The legends drew the attention of young Romantic poets among the Philomaths, especially Adam Mickiewicz, who devoted three ballads to Svitsiaz and the svitsiazianki in his first poetry collection (1822), which made him famous.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini menarik perhatian para penyair romantik muda dari kalangan Filomat, terutama Adam Mickiewicz, yang mempersembahkan tiga balada tentang Svitsiaz dan svitsiazianki dalam kumpulan puisi pertamanya (1822) yang membuatnya terkenal.
claims.quote: прыцягнулі ўвагу маладых паэтаў-рамантыкаў з ліку філаматаў, асабліва Адама Міцкевіча, які прысвяціў Свіцязі і свіцязянкам тры балады ў сваім першым паэтычным зборнік (1822), які зрабіў яго славутым.

claims.statement: In the first ballad the women of the town of Svitsiaz became svitsiazianki when the gods, at their request, drowned the town so they would escape dishonour by the hostile Rus army.
claims.statement_id: Menurut balada pertama, perempuan-perempuan kota Svitsiaz berubah menjadi svitsiazianki ketika kota itu ditenggelamkan para dewa atas permintaan mereka agar terhindar dari aib oleh pasukan Rus yang bermusuhan.
claims.quote: Паводле першай з іх ... у свіцязянак ператварыліся жанчыны горада Свіцязі, затопленага багамі на іх просьбу, каб унікнуць ганьбавання варожым рускім войскам

claims.statement: They were imagined as white-faced girls with long, loose hair.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dibayangkan sebagai gadis-gadis berwajah putih dengan rambut panjang terurai.
claims.quote: Уяўлялі іх як белатварых дзяўчат з даўгімі распушчанымі валасамі.

claims.statement: When the triumphant invaders began to pick the flowers on the lake ("tsary" in Mickiewicz's ballad "Svitsiaz"), they proved poisonous and all of them died.
claims.statement_id: Ketika para penakluk yang berjaya mulai memetik bunga-bunga di danau ("tsary" dalam balada Mickiewicz "Svitsiaz"), bunga itu ternyata beracun dan mereka semua tewas.
claims.quote: Калі трыумфуючыя захопнікі пачалі зрываць кветкі («цары», паводле балады Міцкевіча «Свіцязь»), яны аказаліся атрутнымі, і ўсе яны загінулі.

claims.statement: The second ballad, "Svitsiazianka", tells of the test a svitsiazianka, first posing as an ordinary girl, sets a young hunter in love with her.
claims.statement_id: Balada kedua, "Svitsiazianka", menceritakan ujian yang diberikan seorang svitsiazianka, yang mula-mula menyamar sebagai gadis biasa, kepada seorang pemuda pemburu yang jatuh cinta kepadanya.
claims.quote: Другая балада, «Свіцязянка» ... расказвае пра выпрабаванне, якому свіцязянка, якая спачатку выдае сябе за звычайную дзяўчыну, паддае закаханага ў яе юнака-стральца.

claims.statement: The betrayal was committed, and the soul of the young man, who perishes, is punished with eternal wandering in the surroundings.
claims.statement_id: Pengkhianatan pemuda itu terjadi, dan jiwanya yang binasa dihukum berkelana selamanya di sekitar danau.
claims.quote: Аднак здрада была здзейснена, і душа маладога чалавек, які гіне, пакараная вечным бадзяннем у наваколлі.

claims.statement: Vud-Ava (Meadow Mari Vüd Ava, "Mother of Water") is a goddess of Mari mythology, mistress of all inland waters.
claims.statement_id: Vud-Ava (bahasa Mari Padang: Vüd Ava, "Ibu Air") adalah dewi dalam mitologi Mari, penguasa semua perairan daratan.
claims.quote: (луговомар. Вӱд Ава, Мать воды) — богиня в марийской мифологии, хозяйка всех континентальных водных пространств.

claims.statement: By some accounts she lives in any water, by others only in deep waters; in spring she stirred up silt from the bottom, while in autumn she mixed the water with honey, making it especially tasty.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian keterangan ia tinggal di air mana pun, menurut yang lain hanya di perairan dalam; pada musim semi ia mengaduk lumpur dari dasar, dan pada musim gugur mencampur air dengan madu sehingga terasa sangat enak.
claims.quote: Обитает, по одним данным, в любой воде, по другим, только в глубоких водах. Весной подымала муть со дна, осенью же, напротив, смешивала воду с мёдом, делая её особенно вкусной.

claims.statement: She ensured rich catches and kept the waters clean, forbidding the dumping of slops, washing laundry or making rubbish heaps by rivers, lakes and springs.
claims.statement_id: Ia memberikan tangkapan ikan yang melimpah dan menjaga kebersihan perairan: ia melarang membuang air kotor, mencuci pakaian, dan membuang sampah di dekat sungai, danau, dan mata air.
claims.quote: обеспечивала богатый улов, следила за чистотой водоёмов: запрещала сливать помои, стирать бельё, устраивать свалки у рек, озёр, родников.

claims.statement: Trees near water were never destroyed, as they were considered especially dear to Vud-Ava; the punishment could be losing one's luck in fishing forever.
claims.statement_id: Pohon di dekat air tidak pernah ditebang karena dianggap sangat dicintai Vud-Ava; pelanggarnya bisa dihukum dengan kehilangan keberuntungan memancing untuk selamanya.
claims.quote: Никогда не уничтожались деревья вблизи воды — они считались особо любимыми Вӱд-Авой. За это могло последовать наказание в виде лишения навсегда удачи в рыбалке.

claims.statement: She could "hide" water deep in the taiga: a lake would vanish, and that same year hunters would find an identical new one in the forest.
claims.statement_id: Ia bisa "menyembunyikan" air di kedalaman taiga: sebuah danau lenyap, dan pada tahun yang sama para pemburu menemukan danau baru yang serupa di hutan.
claims.quote: Она могла «спрятать» воду в глубине тайги: озеро исчезало, а в тот же год охотники находили в лесу новое такое же.

claims.statement: The goddess was imagined as a naked woman with long hair, which she likes to comb with a golden comb.
claims.statement_id: Dewi ini dibayangkan sebagai perempuan telanjang berambut panjang yang suka menyisir rambutnya dengan sisir emas.
claims.quote: Богиню представляли в виде обнажённой женщины с длинными волосами, которые она любит расчёсывать золотым гребнем.

claims.statement: Sometimes the goddess could take the form of a pike.
claims.statement_id: Kadang dewi ini bisa mengambil wujud ikan tombak (pike).
claims.quote: Иногда богиня могла принимать образ щуки.

claims.statement: As the ancestress of all things, Vud-Ava was considered the oldest goddess and the embodiment of wisdom.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai leluhur segala sesuatu, Vud-Ava dianggap dewi tertua dan personifikasi kebijaksanaan.
claims.quote: Как родоначальница всего, Вӱд-Ава считалась старейшей богиней, олицетворением мудрости.

claims.statement: Lyuzimer (from "lyuznitny", to scatter something) is a harmful spirit of Komi mythology who rules whirling currents of air and water.
claims.statement_id: Lyuzimer (dari "lyuznitny", menghamburkan sesuatu) adalah roh pengganggu dalam mitologi Komi yang menguasai pusaran udara dan air.
claims.quote: (от люзьнитны — раструсить что-либо) — вредоносный дух в мифологии коми, который заведует вихревыми потоками воздуха, воды.

claims.statement: In winter he is responsible for drifting ground snow, and in summer and autumn for scattering hay from the stacks.
claims.statement_id: Pada musim dingin ia bertanggung jawab atas salju yang tertiup angin di permukaan tanah, dan pada musim panas dan gugur ia menghamburkan jerami dari tumpukannya.
claims.quote: Зимой он ответственен за позёмку, а летом и осенью — размётом сена из стогов.

claims.statement: Tobacco was considered an effective remedy against Lyuzimer; he stopped frolicking in the meadow when that word was spoken.
claims.statement_id: Tembakau dianggap penangkal ampuh terhadap Lyuzimer; ia berhenti bersenang-senang di padang rumput begitu kata itu diucapkan.
claims.quote: Считалось, что действенным средством против Люзимера служит табак. Он переставал веселиться на лугу при произнесении этого слова.

claims.statement: Among the Hindus of the mountainous regions of northern India, the Runiya are a special kind of bhuta demon: demons of avalanches and landslides.
claims.statement_id: Pada orang Hindu di daerah pegunungan India utara, Runiya adalah jenis khusus demon bhuta: demon longsoran salju dan tanah longsor.
claims.quote: индусов гористых местностей северной Индии особый вид демонов-«бхутов» — демоны лавин и обвалов почвы

claims.statement: The Runiya appear at night, riding a huge rock as if it were a horse.
claims.statement_id: Runiya muncul pada malam hari, menunggangi batu karang raksasa seperti menunggang kuda.
claims.quote: Руния являются ночью, восседая верхом на огромной скале, как на лошади.

claims.statement: If a Runiya falls in love with a woman, his spirit comes to her in dreams, and she begins to waste away and dies.
claims.statement_id: Jika Runiya jatuh cinta pada seorang perempuan, rohnya mendatanginya dalam mimpi, dan perempuan itu mulai merana lalu meninggal.
claims.quote: Если Руния полюбит какую-нибудь женщину, то дух его является ей в сновидениях, она начинает чахнуть и умирает.
